title: Tracing a disk change through IGrasp: from notify event to tab, tree and toast
intro: You will be able to follow one edited, replaced, renamed or deleted markdown file from the Rust watcher (`index/watcher.rs`) through the `fs://changes` and `graph://changed` events to the zustand stores that update the tree, tabs, toasts and link flags. You will also know where a fix to this flow goes and which tests, Rust or Vitest, cover it.
subject: Trace it: what happens when a file changes on disk

chapters.title: The watcher: debounce, classify, plan
chapters.goal: Explain how `WatchContext::handle` in `src-tauri/src/index/watcher.rs` turns a debounced `notify` batch into a `Plan` via `classify`: which events are ignored (Access, `.git`, `node_modules`, non-markdown creations), when an ignore file forces `full_rescan`, and what the poll fallback is.
chapters.hootIntro: Before a tab reloads or a toast pops, `index/watcher.rs` has already decided what a burst of raw file events means, so let's watch that decision being made.

steps.title: One debounced batch enters WatchContext::handle
steps.body: `start_watcher` hands `notify_debouncer_full` a closure that calls `WatchContext::handle` once per `DEBOUNCE` window (200 ms). `handle` first bumps `disk_revision`, even for a batch that ends up ignored, because anything computed from the whole folder (the learning profile cache, for example) is now stale. It then reduces each event to a `SimpleEvent`: its `EventKind` plus root-relative paths, with `None` for paths outside the root or non-UTF-8. Only then does it take the index write lock, call `classify` and run `apply_plan`. Events that arrive before the first scan finishes are dropped, since that scan covers them.

stops.annotation: `classify` is a pure function: events, the current `Index`, and a `kind_on_disk` callback (file, folder or gone). The first three rules: skip `Access` events, send any ignore file to `full_rescan`, and pair a `RenameMode::Both` event into `plan.renamed` only when the source is a known file and the target is markdown.

Per path: the root itself and anything under `.git` or `node_modules` (`is_skipped`) is dropped. Known markdown files that were modified go to `plan.modified`, and removals go to `removed_files` or `removed_dirs`. A remove of something the index never knew is ignored.

Everything else (creates, renames, unknown paths) asks the disk. A non-markdown file is skipped, a vanished path is forgotten, and anything else lands in `rewalk`. The final `retain` drops re-walk paths already covered by an outer one, so a new folder is walked once.
The test that pins the ignore rules: a modified `docs/.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude` sets `full_rescan`, while creations under `.git/objects` and `node_modules` produce `Plan::default()`.

steps.title: Where build churn is cut off
steps.prompt: Click the line that makes `classify` ignore a newly created file that is not markdown.
steps.explanation: The `Some(false) if !markdown => {}` arm means the path is a file on disk and not markdown, so it is dropped before it can reach `rewalk`. That is why compiler output or `target/` churn never costs a directory walk. The test `creations_and_new_folders_are_rewalked_but_other_files_skipped` checks it with `src/main.rs`.

steps.question: A Modify event arrives for `.git/info/exclude`. What does `classify` do with it?
choices: It sets `full_rescan` for the whole folder
It drops the path as part of `.git`
It adds the path to `rewalk` only
It adds the path to `modified` only
steps.hint: Compare the order of `is_ignore_file` and `is_skipped` inside the loop, and look at the ignore-rules test.
steps.explanation: `is_ignore_file` matches `.git/info/exclude` explicitly and is tested at the top of the loop, before `is_skipped` would discard `.git` paths. Ignore rules can change which markdown is visible anywhere, so only a full re-index is safe.

steps.title: What each Plan field asks apply_plan to do
steps.prompt: Match each `Plan` field to the work `apply_plan` does for it.

pairs.right: Re-index the whole folder with `index_scope` and diff it against the index
Re-stat the known file and keep it only if its size or mtime changed
Drop the file from the index and report it as removed
Remove the folder and every markdown file under it
Run the ignore-aware walker on that path and diff the result with `diff_within`

steps.explanation: `classify` only decides; `apply_plan` touches the disk and the index. A `modified` entry whose mtime and size are unchanged produces no change, and a `rewalk` goes through the same walker as the full scan, so `.gitignore` still applies to files that appear later.

steps.title: The poll fallback
steps.body: `start_watcher` tries `new_debouncer` with the native watcher first. If creating it or `watch(&root, Recursive)` fails, for example when the Linux inotify limit is reached, it logs a warning and builds a `PollWatcher` debouncer with `POLL_INTERVAL` of 2 s. The handler is the same `WatchContext::handle`, so classification and everything after it are identical. Only the `fs://watch-status` event differs: `WatchMode::Native`, `Poll` with the reason, or `Off` if even polling fails. The status bar's "Polling for changes" text comes from that event.

sources.why: start_watcher with native and poll paths

steps.title: Run the classifier tests
steps.instruction: Run the watcher's unit tests and read their names against the rules in `classify`. Then add `--ignored` to see `real_notifications_reach_the_handler`, which uses real file-system notifications. A name filter skips the ts-rs export tests, so run the full `npm run rust:test` before you commit.
steps.expected: The `index::watcher::tests` cases pass, including `renames_are_paired` and `access_events_are_ignored`; the real-notification test is listed as ignored.

takeaways: `WatchContext::handle` bumps `disk_revision` for every debounced batch, then runs `classify` and `apply_plan` under the index write lock.
`classify` is pure: it skips Access events, `.git`, `node_modules` and non-markdown creations, and an ignore file (`.gitignore`, `.ignore`, `.git/info/exclude`) forces `full_rescan`.
If native watching fails, `start_watcher` falls back to a 2 s `PollWatcher` that feeds the same handler and reports `WatchMode::Poll`.

chapters.title: From plan to `fs://changes`: index diff and the replaced-in-place rule
chapters.goal: Trace `apply_plan` and `Index::diff_within` into `to_event`. Explain why a file removed and added in one batch is reported as `modified`, how `renamed` and `dirsChanged` are derived, and what `generation` guards.

chapters.title: The frontend fan-out: bridge, tabs, tree and toasts
chapters.goal: Follow `fs://changes` through `eventBridge.ts` into `applyDiskChanges` (`diskChanges.ts`): its ordering, `useTree.applyChanges`, `useDocuments.reload` and `revision`, `keepScrollTop`, and the 1.5 s quiet window and grouping in `toasts.ts`.

chapters.title: The graph follow-up and how the flow is tested
chapters.goal: Explain how the batch reaches `graph::apply` and `graph://changed`, how `useGraph.onChanged` refreshes links and backlinks, and how `diskChanges.test.ts` drives the flow with the mock backend (`writeFiles`, `deleteFiles`, `renameFile`, `emit`).
